cards.text: Proverbs starts a new section here, and the teacher talks right to the listener. Incline your ear, the teacher says, and hear the words of the wise, and apply your mind to my knowledge. Friend, that is the oldest way on record of saying PUT THE PHONE DOWN.

cards.question: The teacher says it's pleasing to keep these words within you and also on your lips.

cards.text: Then it gets personal: "I instruct you today—yes, you." YES, YOU, friend, not whoever's on mute in the meeting pretending their camera's broken.

cards.question: The teacher says all this instruction has a goal. What is it?

answers.text: So your trust may be in the LORD
So your name will be remembered
So your barns will be full

cards.text: The teacher has written thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge, to show true and reliable words. THIRTY, friend. I've got ONE saying, "don't open the oven every two minutes," and I can't even keep that one.

cards.question: These true and reliable words will also help the listener soundly answer whom?

cards.text: Now the sayings begin, and the very first one stands up for the little guy. Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate.

cards.question: Don't rob the poor or crush the afflicted at the gate, because the ___ will take up their case.

cards.text: And the LORD will plunder those who rob them. Next saying: do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man.

cards.question: Why steer clear of the hot-tempered man, the guy who honks for three straight miles when somebody cuts him off?

answers.text: You may learn his ways and get caught in a snare
He will spread your secrets and ruin your good name
He will borrow your money and never pay it back

cards.text: Here's one for your wallet: do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts. Somebody slides that paper across the table and says "it's just a formality," and friend, it is NEVER just a formality.

cards.question: If you put up security for a debt and have nothing to pay with, what does the teacher say could be taken?

answers.text: Your own bed from under you
Your seat at the city gate

cards.text: The teacher heads outside now, out to the edge of the family land, where an ancient boundary stone sits right where your fathers placed it. That rock has been sitting there longer than my oldest joke, and friend, that's a LONG time.

cards.question: The teacher says moving that ancient boundary stone is fine if you need more room.

cards.text: Then the teacher asks, "Do you see a man skilled in his work?" Not the one who says "let's circle back" in every meeting, friend, the one who actually gets it DONE.

cards.question: A man skilled in his work won't stand before obscure men. He'll be stationed in the presence of ___.

cards.text: Next up, dinner with a ruler: consider carefully what is set before you, and if you possess a great appetite, put a knife to your throat. That is a STRONG way to say slow down, and I needed it every single time a batch came out of the oven.

cards.question: At the ruler's table, why shouldn't you crave his delicacies?

answers.text: That food is for his servants
That food is set aside for later

cards.text: And now the teacher talks money, and how hard to chase it. Everybody lean in, friend, because I SEE you checking your balance.

cards.question: The teacher says it's worth wearing yourself out to get rich.

cards.text: Then the teacher paints a picture, and friend, it's a wild one. Money. With WINGS.

cards.question: Wealth makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle to the sky. What's the point of that picture?

answers.text: Riches come to whoever chases them

cards.text: I've SEEN that eagle, friend: it hits the account Friday, and by Sunday it's waving down from the clouds like BYE. Then the teacher pulls up a chair at a stingy man's table: do not eat his bread, and do not crave his delicacies.

cards.question: The stingy host tells you, 'Eat and drink.' What's really going on inside him?

answers.text: He's hoping you'll stay all night
He's getting ready to ask a favor

cards.text: His heart is not with you. It's the friend who says "Grab anything you want!" and then sends you a payment request for ONE cookie.

cards.question: At the stingy man's table, the teacher says even your pleasant words go to waste.

cards.text: Then comes a quick one, short enough to stamp on a cookie: do not speak to a fool.

cards.question: Don't speak to a fool, for he will ___ the wisdom of your words.
The boundary stone warning comes back, with something added. Now it also says don't encroach on the fields of whom?
Leave the fields of the fatherless alone, because their Redeemer will take up their case against you. What does the teacher say about their Redeemer?

cards.text: Then the teacher says, "Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge." Back at the start it was ear and mind, and now it's heart and ears.

cards.question: The last saying here turns to raising a child. The teacher says to hold back discipline from a child.

cards.text: The teacher says, "Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol." That's where we'll stop for now, friend, because these thirty sayings are nowhere near done.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says "Everybody lean in, friend," which speaks to a group. He should be talking to one baker.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time.

findings.problem: The card opens with a joke about the eagle, the wealth image from 23:5, but it cites only 23:6. The card uses 23:5, so the citation is too narrow. It should be Proverbs 23:5-6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only one that starts "You may" and the only one with Bible-sounding wording ("get caught in a snare"). Both wrong answers follow the same "He will..." pattern. The right answer stands out as the odd one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says 22:22 is "the very first one" of the thirty sayings. The BSB text doesn't number the sayings or say where the first one starts, and 22:17-21 can be read as part of them. This states as fact something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Verse 23:8's main consequence, "You will vomit up what little you have eaten," is never told on any card. The question says "even your pleasant words go to waste," which hints that something else is lost but never says what. The baker misses the verse's central image.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
